n01.speaker: narrator
n01.text: Last time, this came from software. It also comes from somewhere else.

n02.speaker: narrator
n02.text: Every company can be drawn as a set of functions - the jobs it has to do to create value.

n03.speaker: narrator
n03.text: These are the functions that build the product and get it to a customer - the primary work.

n04.speaker: narrator
n04.text: Underneath, the functions that make the first row possible, without building the product themselves.

n05.speaker: narrator
n05.text: What's left over, once both rows have done their work - the difference between what it cost and what it earned.

n06.speaker: narrator
n06.text: This is a value chain. It says what a company does. It does not yet say how the work actually moves.

n07.speaker: narrator
n07.text: That gap is exactly where this chapter is headed.

n08.speaker: narrator
n08.text: Say this box is where the actual work happens. What does work look like, up close?

n09.speaker: narrator
n09.text: Break work into small, specialized pieces - one worker, one narrow task each. This is Taylorism. It built the industrial revolution.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: On a factory floor, that worked. Each step was simple. A worker didn't need to know what happened before - just do the one thing in front of them.

n11.speaker: narrator
n11.text: Modern work doesn't stay this simple. Each step here needs to know the whole case, not just its own task.

n12.speaker: narrator
n12.text: Every handoff, someone has to reconstruct the context from nothing. That reconstruction - not the task itself - is what actually costs time.

n13.speaker: narrator
n13.text: Combine the small steps back into fewer, wider ones -

n14.speaker: narrator
n14.text: - and give them to people who understand the whole case, not just one narrow piece of it.

n15.speaker: narrator
n15.text: Zoom back out. A company doesn't run on one function. It runs on a handful of processes - and each one stays a closed box.

n16.speaker: narrator
n16.text: None of these are opened up. What matters here is only what crosses the line between them.

n17.speaker: narrator
n17.text: This is as deep as the org level goes - a name, a manager, what comes in, what goes out. Not a flowchart of how the work happens inside.

n18.speaker: narrator
n18.text: Open it further, and you're no longer describing the company - you're describing one process's own internal work. Different question, different level.

n19.speaker: narrator
n19.text: What happens at these lines is, more than almost anything inside the boxes, what the business is actually judged on.

n20.speaker: narrator
n20.text: A shape for what the company does. A reason the work has to be grouped coarser than Taylor would have grouped it. And a boundary around each process that stays deliberately closed.

n21.speaker: narrator
n21.text: Different road than last time. Same destination.
